Gotham is intended, by design, to be an irredeemable and rotten-to-the-core environment. It represents the futility of one man raging against the machine. That's what makes Batman so noble in his endeavors, because we all know that the most effective way, the best way to protect Gotham's civilians, would be to execute Joker and the other Rogue's Gallery to ensure they don't end up killing any more innocents. But if Batman were to do that, he knows with the self-control he has, that he would end up justifying it in every new case he comes across. So he can't bring himself to cross that moral event horizon.

In short, he walks a razor's edge, in the hope that one day, he can clean up Gotham one case at a time before the rot consumes it all. It's a fool's errand, and he's unlikely to succeed, but therein lies the nobility in the struggle, because he must do so without succumbing to the same base urges that infest Gotham so thoroughly.

Joker and Batman, like Harvey Dent and Two-Face, are two sides of the same proverbial coin...all it takes is one bad day to push someone over the edge. The question is, "What will that person do when they snap?" One side became a homicidal maniac, the other one runs around playing dress-up and playing superhero (whilst becoming one in his own right).
